verified_figures.breakout: Wikipedia Cowra breakout: 5 August 1944, 1,104 Japanese POWs escaped (the 1,104/1,104 in research is consistent; use 1,104). 'Largest prison escape of WWII' is in the lead. Leaders ordered no attacks on civilians; none were hurt.

items.fix: Cowra is a town of about 8,000 people on the Lachlan River, around 310 km west of Sydney. During the Second World War it held a prisoner-of-war camp, and on 5 August 1944 more than a thousand Japanese prisoners broke out; the camp site and the Japanese war cemetery beside the town are why many visitors come. The Japanese garden, designed by Ken Nakajima as a strolling garden, symbolises reconciliation and peace after the war. Cowra is also the base for a wine region of over 40 vineyards around Cowra, Billimari and Canowindra.
items.note: Cut 'The town's response was a Japanese garden': no source links the garden to the Breakout (it says reconciliation after WWII; Wikivoyage adds 'and after the local conflict', but that is thin). 'The sites left from that night' reworded to 'camp site'. 310 km is by road (Wikipedia) so 'around 310 km' is fine. Population: Wikipedia 8,254, 'about 8,000' is acceptable. Nakajima is on the garden site's address and Wikivoyage; kaiyu-shiki is Wikivoyage.

items.fix: Cowra sits on the Lachlan River in the Central West, 310 km west of Sydney and 189 km north of Canberra (both by road), where the Mid-Western Highway, Olympic Highway and Lachlan Valley Way meet. It is best known for two things from the Second World War: the 1944 prisoner-of-war breakout, and the Japanese garden, designed to symbolise reconciliation and peace. The Japanese war cemetery on Doncaster Drive is the only one in Australia. Beyond the town, over 40 vineyards around Cowra, Billimari and Canowindra make it a wine base, and Canowindra lies 32 km north.
items.note: Original said the garden AND cemetery 'stand for peace'; only the garden is sourced that way. Other facts (310 km, 189 km, three highways, only Japanese war cemetery, 40+ vineyards, 32 km) verified. Preferred variant, with this fix.

items.fix: Cowra is a Lachlan River town of around 8,000 where the Mid-Western Highway, Olympic Highway and Lachlan Valley Way meet. It was the site of a Second World War prisoner-of-war camp, and the breakout of 5 August 1944 is the largest prison escape of the war. Visitors can walk the camp site, visit the Japanese and Australian war cemeteries on Doncaster Drive, and stroll the 12.5-acre Japanese garden, which its operator calls the largest in the Southern Hemisphere. Cherry blossom fills the garden in spring, and April brings the Balloon Challenge to Canowindra, 32 km north.
